title: Tree of Heaven: Old Ailanthus Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: The species cities spend the most money removing, and all four of these are protected or plaqued instead. Four mapped, the largest in Ireland included.
intro: Ailanthus altissima is the tree cities spend the most money getting rid of, and all four of these are protected or plaqued instead. The one in Ravenscourt Park in London has a green plaque at its foot. Zaragoza lists the specimen in its botanical garden as a singular tree. Dublin's is the largest in Ireland, framed between two Victorian glasshouses, and its age is a real argument: the register says 120 to 165 years, the way this species grows suggests closer to 70 or 100. That growth rate is the whole problem with it. Tree of heaven seeds into any crack, sends suckers under pavement and shades out whatever stood there first, fast enough to reach a serious size within one lifetime. The Danish name says what that looks like: skyraekker, sky reacher. Copenhagen's, in Assistens, is 15.5 metres.
